learning_outcomes.text: Understand, evaluate and analyze the different forms of representation and simplification of logical functions, as well as mastering the most common numbering systems used in digital.
Analyze, simulate and synthesize combinational circuits, and select the most appropriate technology according to the initial specifications.
Simulate and design asynchronous and synchronous sequential circuits, based on given specifications, as well as detect faults in circuits and propose appropriate solutions in each case.

Implement complete low-medium complexity systems, including sequential/combinational circuits and appropriate I/O stages; select the most suitable commercial components, from technical and economic points of view, all based on a problem specified by a client.
Work in a group, reason critically to compare various solutions and discriminate the most optimal one.
Implement circuit designs in a structured way, dividing them into simpler sub-circuits and their subsequent integration into a superior one, based on given specifications.

syllabus_topics: Representation of binary numbers with and without sign
Interface between TTL and CMOS families
Synthesis of combinational circuits with logic gates
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum score of 4.0 out of 10 is required in the theoretical block. The final theory grade is 60% of the final exam. The final practical grade is 10% of (P1 + P2). The final works grade is 4% of (T1 + T2 + T3 + T4 + T5). The final course grade is the sum of Theory, Practices, and Works, but if the minimum in theory is not reached, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. For the extraordinary call of June/July, theory requires a minimum of 4 points, and practical and work scores are carried over. For the extraordinary call of December/January, there is a theoretical exam (minimum 4 points) and a practical exam (no minimum required); the final grade is 60% Theory and 40% Practical, with the same minimum rule as above.
